payload.claim: `cut_off = any("error_max_turns" in e for e in turns_row.endings)` detects a cut-off attempt only through the `subtype` string embedded in `endings` (line 1245); it never checks `terminal_reason` independently. `saffron/cell/session.py`'s `cut_off_at_turn_ceiling` (line 384) deliberately ORs `terminal_reason == "max_turns"` with `subtype == "error_max_turns"` because backlog item 34 measured a real ledger row where the two fields diverged ("a result event arriving without the one field would have skipped the salvage in silence"). If a past attempt has `terminal_reason="max_turns"` but a `subtype` other than `error_max_turns`, `endings` will contain e.g. `"IMPLEMENTING unknown (max_turns)"`, the substring `"error_max_turns"` will not match, and the `ceilings:` line will report that row's peak as `used` instead of `a floor` — silently reintroducing, for this new comparison, the exact single-field fragility the codebase already found and fixed once for the salvage-turn check.
